title: Пьяный Шеф увольняет всех  (The Drunken Chef Fires Everyone)

segments.t: After polishing off the cognac inside the cold storage room, Chef Barinov emerges furious and drunk, paying Fedya back his debt only to fire him and the rest of the kitchen crew on the spot. Lyova reassures everyone that the Chef will sleep it off in two hours and forget everything.
Федя, я тебе все долги вернул?
Ну и пошел вон с моей кухни.
Все, кому я не сказал, что они уволены.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Write it yourself.' In Russian, the idea of 'yes' flows naturally into 'himself' without extra filler words. Fedya answers right away.
Федя, я тебе все долги вернул?
'Fedya, have I paid back all my debts to you?' Fedya brings out the contrast between 'Fedya' and 'I' in a few short words.
Ну и пошел вон с моей кухни.
'Then get the hell out of my kitchen.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'come on', while 'cuisine' completes the thought.
'Pick up the oranges and you are fired immediately.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'to collect' and finishing on 'fired'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'Oh, and one more thing.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'yes' and 'both' in a few short words.
Все, кому я не сказал, что они уволены.
'Everyone else whom I have not yet told that they are fired.' Fedya anchors the line on 'all', while 'to fire' completes the thought.
'And what are we supposed to do now?' Notice how Russian expresses 'both' and 'what is one to do' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Fedya answers right away.
'Calm down, all of you.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'yes' and finishing on 'you'.
'In two hours it will wear off.' In Russian, the idea of 'two' flows naturally into 'to let go' without extra filler words.
'He will not remember a thing.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'he' and finishing on 'will remember'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'What are you hiding behind your back?' The grammar packs 'what' and 'hide' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'The Chef has had enough already.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'chef' and finishing on 'now'.

'You talked me into it, I will drink it myself.' The plural past ending '-li' on the verb for 'persuade' covers a group or the polite 'you'. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
Федя, я тебе все долги вернул?
Ну и пошел вон с моей кухни.
Все, кому я не сказал, что они уволены.
That wraps up this scene as after drinking the cognac in the walk-in fridge, Chef Barinov stumbles out, fires Fedya and the entire kitchen staff on the spot, and passes out. Until next time!
